speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your episodes of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing, could you describe exactly what happens right before an episode starts, and how long these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: That muddy taste suggests an olfactory aura, which strongly points to temporal lobe involvement. I would like to request an EEG to look for epileptiform activity and an MRI of the brain to rule out any structural abnormalities like a tumor or hippocampal sclerosis. REQUEST TEST: EEG. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain.
